intro: Business and market vocabulary, and how to imagine what would have happened if things had been different.

palabras.consejo: It comes from «emprender». There are large, medium and small companies («pymes»).
Feminine: «socia». A partner puts money or work into the company. You can also be a club member.
The secondary offices are «sucursales». You also hear «la sede de un congreso».
A bank or a shop has its headquarters in one place and branches in others.
It goes with «oferta»: «la oferta y la demanda». You say «hay mucha demanda» or «poca demanda».
Two meanings: «la oferta y la demanda» and «estar de oferta», which is to be on sale.
In business they are the rivals. A sports race is «una competición». It also means «skill».
You say «hacer un pedido» and «recibir un pedido». It comes from «pedir».
It comes from «proveer»: to supply what is needed. A supplier delivers goods to a shop.
It comes from «lanzar». You say «el lanzamiento de un producto» or «de un libro».
It is also a mark on something: «una marca en la pared». You say «una marca conocida».
It works for masculine and feminine: «un negocio rentable», «una tienda rentable».
It also means «advantage»: «un beneficio para todos». Its financial opposite is «pérdida».
The e becomes ie: «quiebro», «quiebras», «quiebra». A company that goes bankrupt closes.
From «vender», to sell; the «v» sounds like «b».
Plural of «zapatilla»; the «z» sounds like «th» in Spain.
Feminine plural of «barato», agreeing with «zapatillas».
Used after «si» for something that did not happen: «si hubiéramos esperado».
Past participle of «lanzar», to launch something.
Past participle of «enviar», to send; the «v» sounds like «b».
Goods for sale; in Spain the «cí» sounds like «thi».
«Negocio» is a business; «negociar» means to negotiate.
Plural of «socio», a partner in a business.
Subjunctive of «quebrar», to go bankrupt, after «que».
Like «hubiéramos», used after «si» for something that did not happen.
In «hacer caso», it means to pay attention to advice.
Conditional of «haber» for «ellos»: what would have happened.
«Producto» comes from «producir», to make.
Subjunctive of «tener» in «si» sentences: if we had.
Conditional of «abrir» for «nosotros»: what we would do.
The «j» sounds like «h» in «garaje».
«Goma» is rubber, the stretchy material.
From «pegar», to stick; «pegamento» is what makes things stick.
Imperfect of «cortar» for «ellos»: an action going on in the past.
Plural of «botella»; the «ll» sounds like «y».
Imperfect of «coser», to sew; the accent on «í» gives two syllables.
Plural of «suela», the bottom part of a shoe.
«Grueso» means thick; its opposite is «fino».
«Aquellas» points to far away things, feminine plural.
Imperfect of «contar» for «ellos»: something repeated in the past.
Plural of «pérdida», something lost.
Past participle of «encoger», to shrink; «corazón encogido» means a heavy heart.
«Actriz» is the feminine of «actor».
Past tense of «posar», to pose for a photo; the «ó» takes the stress.
«Un par de» means a pair of something.
A «chispa» is a tiny spark that jumps from fire or metal.
Imperfect of «sonar», to ring: it went on in the past.
Plural of «pedido», an order for goods.
Imperfect of «llegar» for «ellos»: going on for a while.
Plural of «montón», a big pile of things.
Past tense of «hacer» for «nosotros»; the «c» sounds like «th».
Plural of «empresa», a company or firm.
«Rival» means competing: the other company after the same customers.
Third person plural in the past of «recibir»; the «c» sounds like «th».
Imperfect of «poder» for «ellos»: what they were able to do.
Infinitive of «atender», to serve or look after customers.

texto:
**The company.** A **empresa** has a **sede** and sometimes **sucursales**. It is formed by one or more **socios**. Its **marca** is the name the public knows it by.

**The market.** **Oferta** is what is offered; **demanda**, what people want to buy. **La competencia** are the rival companies. A business is **rentable** if it makes **beneficios**; if not, it loses money and may **quebrar**.

**Buying and selling.** A shop places a **pedido** with its **proveedor**, who sends the goods. A new product needs a **lanzamiento**, usually with an advertising campaign.

**If I had… I would have…** To talk about what did not happen we use **si + hubiera + participle** and **habría + participle**: **Si hubiéramos lanzado la marca antes, habríamos tenido menos competencia.**

piezas.titulo: What did not happen: if I had… I would have…
texto:
**Si + hubiera/hubiese + participle, habría + participle** talks about something that did not happen and its imagined result: **Si hubiéramos lanzado la marca antes, habríamos tenido menos competencia.** (We did not launch earlier and had more competition.)

- **Hubiera** and **hubiese** are equivalent: **si hubiese hecho** or **si hubiera hecho**.
- After **si** the conditional is never used: you do not say «si habríamos esperado».
- For something unreal in the present, **si + imperfect subjunctive, conditional**: **Si tuviéramos más socios, abriríamos otra sucursal.**

ejemplos.estudio: Si hubieran hecho caso al estudio, nunca habrían lanzado el producto.
ejemplos.alumno: If they had listened to the research, they would never have launched the product.
analisis: Si hubieran hecho caso al estudio nunca habrían lanzado el producto
Si hubieran hecho caso al estudio

opciones.explicacion: Yes: si + hubiéramos + participle, habríamos + participle.

opciones.texto: Si habríamos esperado, habríamos perdido clientes

The second part needs the conditional perfect.

opciones.explicacion: It can mean skill, but a skill does not sell anything.
Yes: in the market, «la competencia» are the rival companies.
Yes: de + article + que, agreeing with «pedidos» (masculine plural).
Before a verb you need «de los que».

opciones.explicacion: «Quebrar» is to run out of money and close.
